new_statements.rule_in_words: Smythe assigns Tulu and Bohuai to his 'Group 3' (all eastern Admiralty / Manus languages), for which the table gives the main position of accent as the final syllable. This is a group-level typological characterisation, not a language-specific rule. The only language-specific primary evidence opened (Blust's 1975 Pelipowai field transcriptions) marks stress predominantly on the word-initial syllable of citation forms (penultimate in disyllables, initial in several trisyllables), with final stress on some singular-possessed and a few other forms, so the two sources do not agree and no rule for Tulu-Bohuai itself can be stated from what was read.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated. (Blust's fieldnotes show an occasional grave mark, e.g. kálopòpwas, cáncpòhow, suggesting a secondary prominence two syllables after the primary; no prose.)
new_statements.exceptions: None in Smythe for Group 3 accent (the table notes segmental exceptions 'except in Ponam', 'except in Sisi' only).
new_statements.domain_note: Smythe's row is 'main position of accent' at the level of his phonetic Group 3 (some two dozen languages), presumably word-level in citation forms; he separately marks 'tones: + in some dialects' for the group. Not a statement about Tulu-Bohuai words specifically.
new_statements.identity_note: Ethnologue/Glottolog 'Tulu-Bohuai' [rak] joins Bohuai (= Pohowa, Pahavai, Bowai; villages Bohuai, Kupano, Pelipowai/Peli Is., south-central Manus) with Tulu (Tjudun/Tulun, north coast) and Keli; Healey 1976 and Schooling & Schooling 1988 instead grouped Tulu with Levei (Levei-Tulu, cf. Khehek khe = kheh1237), and Ethnologue notes rak is 'reportedly similar to Khehek'. Newman's materials (PARADISEC JN2) and Blust's 1975 packet describe the Pohowa/Pelipowai (Bohuai) variety specifically; Smythe's 1970 data point is labelled 'Tulu'. The Blust 2021 Likum sketch quoted for context is a different language (Likum, West Manus II), not tulu1259.

Handwritten phonetic transcriptions carry frequent stress marks, predominantly word-initial (e.g. 'toloh 'three', 'limeh 'five', kánaw, cólah; trisyllables kálamak, mámarow, nóhonoh, kářahak, cákaliy, kácohek, mútuwaw; secondary grave in kálopòpwas), with a few final-stressed forms (pisíw, puwáy, yahá?, lámu pulák; margin [pul'ak]/[pul'an] for possessed 'head'). Primary data only, my reading of low-res scans.
